name: decide which line passes in front at each crossing
one_line: A line figure whose crossings can be resolved several ways, and the question is how many of those ways make a buildable solid.
how: Ask for a 4 cm square, a second the same size shifted 18 mm up and 18 mm right, and the four pairs of corners joined: a transparent cube with two crossings inside it. At each crossing one edge of a real cube would pass in front, so ask for both to be broken all four ways — front and front, front and back, back and front, back and back — and all four figures drawn. Two are cubes; two are not, and look ordinary. Then three beams closed into a triangle, and a table saying A passes in front of B, B of C, C of A. Ask for the beams to be numbered 1, 2, 3 by distance so that all three rows hold. Twenty-seven ways, none works.

knobs.knob: how far the second square is shifted
knobs.effect: anywhere between a twentieth and nineteen twentieths of the side gives the two crossings the exercise rests on; at a full side a back corner lands on a front one and the crossings vanish.

knobs.knob: whether the four figures are drawn or only named
knobs.effect: drawn, the two impossible ones exist on paper and go on looking ordinary as long as anybody stares; named in a table, the answer is right, nothing was made, and the second half has no material.

knobs.knob: whether the beams are numbered or just argued about
knobs.effect: numbering forces the contradiction into three rows a finger can follow; arguing lets «it just can't work» stand as an answer, and that sentence is the one the sheet exists to replace.
two crossings and four resolutions leave two consistent readings; three beams and three rows leave none out of twenty-seven, which is an impossibility proved on a drawing they made themselves.

where_the_work_is: In the table of who passes in front of whom. The drawing is copied in four minutes; the table turns «this looks wrong» into three statements that cannot all hold at once.
breaks: The figure is drawn by hand from two measurements, so the print scale does not matter — the 18 mm shift does, and at a full side length the crossings degenerate. Both counts, two of four and none of twenty-seven, can be marked; what nothing catches is a cube whose corners were joined to the wrong partners, which gives crossings the table does not describe. On the display 800×480 in one bit draws the finished cube well and cannot hold the four erasures, which are the exercise.
